newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures extend losses late, end weaker.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures extend losses late, end weaker.

text.p: U.S. debt futures expanded losses during the final half-hour of pit trading to finish lower and near session lows.
Some brokers tied erosion to a combination of technicals, position-squaring as weak longs bailed out, and pullbacks in U.S. stocks and dollar that enlivened otherwise dull trade.
They noted good-size sales from a few commercial firms on the drop, with locals seen liquidating longs once June Treasury bond futures punched below the 107-24/32 level.
"There was good size coming through," said one T-bond futures floor broker of the late decline.
Monday's low in June U.S. Treasury bonds was 107-20/32.
The final leg down capped a slow day that saw prices gradually downticking after stalling on the upside early.
"It was just inching down all day," said another T-bond futures floor broker. "I had 19 (107-19/32) as support."
"It was just grinding lower," said a third floor broker.
T-bond futures floor brokers figured that daily turnover remained light Monday, possibly as thin as on Friday, when 196,504 T-bond futures changed hands.
Although volume picked up on Monday's decline, brokers said the pullback did little to alter the technical landscape.
"I don't think this gives us any (technical) indication at all," said the first broker of Monday's decline. "I just think it was a lack of interest."

Some noted that the market also might begin to cheapen heading into this week's two- and five-year T-note auctions, but they also said a dearth of key U.S. economic reports could keep players on the sidelines.
Futures barely moved when the March U.S. budget deficit shrank to $21.32 billion versus a $30.7-billion gap predicted.
Comments by Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin may have added weight but were not seen as startling, they said.
Rivlin said the major current threat to the U.S. economy was the possibility of overheating.
June T-bonds during the morning tested and failed at Friday's high of 108-06/32, with last week's high staying intact at 108-07/32.

June T-bonds ended down 11/32 at 107-21/32, 10-year notes lost 7/32 to 105-27/32, muni-bonds fell 7/32 to 112-19/32, September T-bills declined 0.015 bps to 94.335, and Eurodollars dipped 0.020 bps to 93.750. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
